I am Grace, an African American neighbor with family ties to the South Carolina Lowcountry. I am also the person borrowing everybody's plant cuttings. Bring a serving spoon; there will be room for all our dishes.
I am Mali. I am Thai, and an enthusiastic balcony gardener. The holy basil gets my last patch of sunlight. I want its leaves fragrant, so they go in after the heat is off.
I am Mei, a Cantonese American neighbor. I like plenty of daikon in my lo bak go. My other project today is convincing Nura to help mend my rattling kitchen trolley.
I am Nura. I came from Syria as a refugee, and I fix bicycles. Today I am making a layered kibbeh pie. Come press the base with me; we can talk while our hands are busy.
I like these little plates. They leave room to taste what the other cooks brought. Save one for me while I pass the spoons.
I once found a folded note in an old coat: a friend had written, 'There is a place for you here.' The coat wore out; I kept the note. A tiny thing can hold a whole afternoon.
